subject: Voyant pilot: data-use controls, no-train architecture & subprocessor mapping
messages:
From: Elena Rojas <elena@voyanthealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on data use / subprocessors for Voyant pilot

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — excited to move the pilot forward. Before we kick off the technical onboarding, legal and security have a couple of blocking questions and asked me to get them clarified up-front: 

1) No-train / model improvement: we need a contractual commitment that Voyant data (including prompts and responses) will not be used to improve or retrain any shared hosted models. Is that supported for a pilot? If not, what technical/operational controls can you provide to make sure our data is excluded?

2) Prompt/response IP: can you confirm Redwood's position on ownership/derivative rights for prompt/response pairs generated during the integration? We need language that ensures output isn't treated as Redwood-owned derivatives.

3) Subprocessors & data flow: we require an inventory of subprocessors (with locations) and an explanation of any cross-border transfers. We also need to know where audit logs and telemetry live and whether we can receive an export (SFTP preferred).

4) Evidence & timeline: SOC 2 Type II report and a sample subprocessor attestation would help speed legal review. Also please confirm expected timeline to provide necessary DPA edits and a DocuSign for execution.

I've attached a short list of our security questions to this thread. Happy to schedule a quick call.

Best,
Elena
Head of Partnerships
Voyant Health

[Attachment: Voyant_DPA_Questions.docx]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rojas <elena@voyanthealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on data use / subprocessors for Voyant pilot

Hi Elena — great to hear, and thanks for sending the security checklist. Below is a concise mapping of how Redwood handles the items you called out and a proposed next step list. I'm copying Laura (CS) to coordinate timeline.

Quick answers:
- No-train/model-improvement: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support a contractual "no-learning" commitment that prevents customer data from being used to update any model weights or centralized training datasets. For Hosted customers we offer a "no-learn" routing to isolated model variants in some cases, but a full contractual no-train on shared hosted tiers is operationally constrained. For the pilot we recommend Dedicated capacity (or Private) if you require contractual no-train.

- Technical controls we will provide: per-customer KV cache isolation, request-level headers to mark data as no-train, an ops flag that disables telemetry forwarding to model improvement pipelines, and a documented SFTP export path for logs/exports.

- Prompt/response IP: Redwood's standard DPA/Terms state customers retain rights to their input and generated outputs. To avoid ambiguity we can add a short DPA addendum clarifying "no-derivative" and explicit customer ownership of outputs for Voyant.

- Subprocessors & transfers: attached is our current subprocessor inventory (exported 2027-06-18) — includes region and function (monitoring, storage, telemetry). For Dedicated/Private we can route storage to an EU/US region depending on your preference and provide subprocessor attestations.

Attachments I added: redwood-subprocessors-inventory-20270618.xlsx; no-train-ops-checklist.pdf (ops steps we follow to demonstrate isolation).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Legal: Karthik to propose DPA language/addendum (we'll provide wording).
2) Infra: Enable a dedicated capacity environment for the pilot and toggle the no-train ops flag (ETA 3 business days after sign-off).
3) Ops: Prepare evidence pack (SOC2 cert, subprocessor attestations, dataflow diagram) and SFTP export endpoint — we'll provide credentials and retention window options.
4) DocuSign: Once Karthik and Voyant legal agree wording, we'll route a DPA addendum via DocuSign.

We'll treat export of audit logs as a 30-day retention window by default, but we can extend to 13 months to match your ask (requires a minor storage configuration).

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk legal/security through the inventory and ops checklist — I can bring our infra lead.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-inventory-20270618.xlsx, no-train-ops-checklist.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on data use / subprocessors for Voyant pilot

Elena / team — adding a few specific clauses that typically close these asks quickly. Quoting Mateo below for context.

Suggested DPA addendum bullets (high level):
- No-Learning Commitment: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data (including prompts and outputs) to train or improve any shared third-party or Redwood-managed model for the duration of the agreement, except as required to provide the Service to Customer and as set forth in an agreed schedule of permitted uses."
- Output Rights / Derivatives: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data and any Outputs generated therefrom. Redwood shall not assert ownership over Outputs nor use Outputs for derivative model training without explicit written consent."
- Subprocessor Attestation: Redwood will provide an inventory and attest to the subset of subprocessors that will process Customer Data; Redwood will provide SOC2 Type II and reasonable evidence of controls for subprocessors upon request.
- Export & Logs: Redwood will provide a daily audit-log export accessible via SFTP with retention configurable between 30 days and 13 months per Customer request.

Operational note: when we commit to 13-month retention we need to ensure encryption-at-rest keys are accounted for in our KMS grant flow; Ops will need a short task to map retention to billing.

I'll draft a one-page addendum (DPA_clause_suggestions.docx) and circulate for signature.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
